Auxetic Grip Pad — a rotating-rigid-squares metamaterial sheet.
 WHAT IT IS A flat sheet of rigid square tiles, each joined to its four edge-neighbours at ONE corner only, and that corner alternates in a checkerboard so neighbouring tiles are forced to counter-rotate. Pull the sheet in one direction and every tile twists, which also opens the gaps the other way: it expands on BOTH axes at once. That is a negative Poisson ratio (about -1). A normal sheet necks in when you stretch it; this one fattens.
 WHY IT GRIPS Because it has a negative Poisson ratio it goes synclastic: drape it over a jar lid, a bottle cap or any dome and it forms a cap that hugs the curve instead of wrinkling, so far more of the pad touches the surface. The open lattice and tile edges bite into a lid's knurling. Pull to conform, release to grip. It also makes a satisfying flexible fidget sheet.
